name: Giancarlo Bodoni Turtle to Back System
description: Explore Giancarlo Bodoni Turtle to Back System with a matched BJJ Fanatics course, practical study steps, partner drills, and connected technique references.
summary: The Giancarlo Bodoni Turtle to Back System is a study framework for turning a rear ride into stable back control while accounting for hooks and stand-up attempts.
overview:
A visible back is an opportunity to establish control, but it does not guarantee that hooks or a finish are available. This guide studies the gap between following a turtled opponent and securing a usable rear position. Giancarlo Bodoni's Behind The Elbows course is the selected companion because its syllabus distinguishes turtle shapes, hook insertion, breakdowns and four-point stand-ups. That makes it a focused complement to the site's guides on finishing once back control is already established.

The sequence and drills below are original BJJGraph study suggestions, not a course transcript or an official instructor curriculum. Use the linked demonstrations for technical detail, then compare one selected lesson with a controlled partner round.
key_principles: Identify whether the elbows and knees offer access before deciding where to establish the initial ride.
Choose one demonstrated breakdown and stop when the partner loses the intended support rather than continuing into a submission.
Study one near-side or far-side hook route and keep chest-to-back contact through the change.
Let the partner raise their hips into a four-point stance and examine how the ride and control objective change.
Complete the chosen back-control route and add hand fighting only after the partner can test the landing.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Jumping for both hooks without a stable ride
common_obstacles.solution: Practise the first hook and the connection that supports it.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Using the same breakdown against every turtle shape
common_obstacles.solution: Name which support the partner is offering before choosing the direction.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Ignoring the transition to four points
common_obstacles.solution: Introduce that response as a separate stage rather than treating it as an accidental scramble.

common_obstacles.obstacle: Measuring progress only by rear naked chokes
common_obstacles.solution: Track whether the partner can turn or stand before counting an attacking result.

training_methodology.drilling_approach: BJJGraph practice suggestion: start from Turtle and give the partner one agreed response. Work through the first two stages cooperatively, then stop each repetition at the chosen control or recovery endpoint. Add another reaction only when both partners can explain what changed. Keep submission entries controlled and release immediately on a tap or request to stop. Review the lost connection before adding speed.

products.title: Essential Connections: Chest To Back - Behind The Elbows
products.blurb: A directly matched instructional companion for turning a rear ride into stable back control while accounting for hooks and stand-up attempts. Review its published contents and sample to judge the teaching approach.
products.best_for: No-gi players who get behind turtle but lose opponents during hook insertion or stand-up attempts.
products.study_focus: Compare closed and open turtle, then the near-hook and far-hook pathways; review the stand-up and four-point material once the basic ride is familiar.
products.practice_tip: BJJGraph suggestion: begin with 'Read the turtle shape' from Turtle. Record which partner response interrupts the plan and revisit that lesson before adding another branch.
